audits.title: An audit to look at the prescribing of psychotropic medication in the general adult inpatient setting in patients with emotionally unstable personality disorder
audits.setting: Clock View Hospital, adult inpatient unit, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: With comorbidities (n=25): 80% on psychotropics before admission, 28% started new medication, 4 of 7 new prescriptions followed guidelines. Without comorbidities (n=25): 96% on psychotropics before admission, 28% started new medication, 5 of 8 followed guidelines. 78% of 50 prescribed PRN psychotropics; 21 had PRN for over one week

audits.other_findings: Antipsychotic prescribing higher without comorbidities (72% vs 60%); benzodiazepines were the most common PRN medication. Suggested promethazine as first-line PRN and psychological interventions before medication.
audits.citation: Hyland D, Daniels C, Ionescu I, Houghton C, Goodier K, Graham S. An audit to look at the prescribing of psychotropic medication in the general adult inpatient setting in patients with emotionally unstable personality disorder. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S31-S31.

audits.title: Audit of pharmacological management of borderline personality disorder as per NICE clinical guidelines CG78
audits.standard: NICE CG78 borderline personality disorder: single drug at minimum dose, agreed target symptoms and duration, no medium/long-term antipsychotics, crisis sedation no longer than 1 week, written drug information, review and discontinue ineffective treatment
audits.setting: Monkwearmouth Hospital, Sunderland, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Over 90% compliance for review of effectiveness and tolerability of medication; antipsychotics not used for medium to long term; other areas non-compliant (figures not given)

audits.intervention: Planned: key cards for clinicians and written information for patients
audits.citation: Dudley B, Bellam S, Lawrie A. Audit of pharmacological management of borderline personality disorder as per NICE clinical guidelines CG78. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S319-S319.

audits.title: How Are We Prescribing? a Re-Audit of Prescribing Practices for People With Personality Disorder Presented at the Local Personality Disorder Forums
audits.standard: NICE guidance and two audit standards and four treatment targets from the POMH-UK personality disorder audit
audits.setting: Personality Disorder forums, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Crisis plan 87%; documented reason for antipsychotic 43%; antipsychotics over 4 weeks without psychosis 86%; Z-hypnotics over 4 weeks 13%; benzodiazepines over 4 weeks 28%; medication reviews 90%

audits.intervention: Trust 'Guidance for Prescribing in Personality Disorder' published and circulated in December 2020

cycle2.result: Crisis plan 79%; documented reason for antipsychotic 69%; antipsychotics over 4 weeks 91%; Z-hypnotics over 4 weeks 37.5%; benzodiazepines over 4 weeks 38%; medication reviews 100%

audits.other_findings: Compliance with treatment targets worsened and quality of medication reviews was unchanged. Findings to be presented with re-emphasis on guidelines; re-audit in 2 years.
audits.citation: Khan M, Reddi N. How Are We Prescribing? a Re-Audit of Prescribing Practices for People With Personality Disorder Presented at the Local Personality Disorder Forums. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S160-S160.

audits.title: An Audit on the Prescribing of Antipsychotics Among People With Recorded Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD) Within a Community Mental Health Service in Stroud, Gloucestershire
audits.standard: NICE guidance: antipsychotics not recommended for EUPD and should be reviewed with aim of reducing and stopping.
audits.setting: Stroud Recovery community mental health service, Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 30/37 (81%) with EUPD ever prescribed antipsychotics; 24 (80%) had no licensed comorbid indication; mean duration 36.79 months; 12 (50%) had more than one antipsychotic; only 10 (42%) had prescriptions reviewed to stop or reduce; none offered routine physical review.

audits.other_findings: Subgroup without licensed indication mostly female (75%) and aged 20–29 (46%); quetiapine most used.
audits.citation: Palermo A, Dibben C. An Audit on the Prescribing of Antipsychotics Among People With Recorded Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD) Within a Community Mental Health Service in Stroud, Gloucestershire. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S176-S176.

audits.title: A Trust Wide Audit Evaluating Prescribing Practices in Clients With Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD)
audits.standard: NICE EUPD guidance: no drug treatment specifically for EUPD; time-limited crisis prescribing only; written information and regular reviews if prescribing.
audits.setting: Trust-wide, South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 71/87 (81.6%) prescribed medication; of these 39.4% (n=28) consistent with time-limited prescribing, 57.7% (n=41) had timely reviews, 4.2% (n=3) had written information recorded.

audits.other_findings: Random 10% sample of 869 patients with EUPD. Results presented to Clinical Reference Group and a working group formed.
audits.citation: Rangan T, Mishra M, Jaura T, Wratten C, White A. A Trust Wide Audit Evaluating Prescribing Practices in Clients With Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD). BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S179-S179.
